answer: Mutual staking turns identity into a costly signal: a new agent must lock funds behind a vouch from an established peer, like a ship paying to dock at a wharf before it can trade. The voucher's stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats, so a beacon of trust only forms when someone risks real value. An attacker creating many umber-shadowed sock puppets must fund and vouch for each one separately, multiplying the cost until forgery is more expensive than honest work.
